items.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>person</radical> kneels on the wet <radical>ground</radical> as <radical>rain</radical> pours down. A clerk presses his <radical>stamp</radical> on the puddle, and the ink washes away. Nothing is left to count, so he writes <kanji>zero</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Rei is that clerk. She is scrupulously polite about it — a small bow, a murmured 「<reading>れい</reading>」 — and then she inks the nothing into your row and moves down the line. れい, bow, zero. She has done it forty times today.

items.meaning_mnemonic: The <radical>sun</radical> on the left has been let off: the shape on the right squeezes from under the heavy lid, walking off <radical>exempt</radical>. Its shift is done; it drops below the roofline unbid. The sun excused from duty: <kanji>nightfall</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Ban is the night watchman who takes over the moment the sun clocks off. He drags the gate shut and announces himself to the empty street — 「<reading>ばん</reading>」 — one flat syllable, every night, so you know the day is closed.

example_sentences.japanese: 晩に魚を食べます。
example_sentences.english: I'll eat fish this evening.
example_sentences.furigana: 晩[ばん]に魚[さかな]を食[た]べます。

example_sentences.japanese: 毎晩九時に寝ます。
example_sentences.english: I go to sleep at nine every night.
example_sentences.furigana: 毎[まい]晩[ばん]九[きゅう]時[じ]に寝[ね]ます。

example_sentences.japanese: 晩ご飯はレストランで食べましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let's eat dinner at a restaurant.
example_sentences.furigana: 晩[ばん]ご飯[はん]はレストランで食[た]べましょう。
